Hurricane Isaias Advisory #16
Effective: October 8, 2026 1600 CDT
Active Storm Advisory
Forecast Discussion
Current Conditions
Satellite
Recent satellite imagery shows that Isaias continues to
improve as convection continues to expand away from the
core, especially to the north where outflow is the
strongest. The center of the storm is attempting to form
an eye, as cloud coverage is beginning to become
shallower over the core. Rough seas extend up to 125nm
in all directions from the core, with very rough to
borderline high seas near the core and maximum wave
heights up to 7.3m (24 feet) currently seen. The maximum
wind speed is currently around 85 knots.
Isaias remains in a favorable environment to develop further, empowered by the very warm seas and abundant moisture
present in the southern Gulf of America. The storm is well ventilated as well, with strong outflow further aiding in the
storms continuing intensification. This trend expected to last for another 12 hours or so before the storms northward
motion begins to cause issues as it enters a region of much stronger wind shear due to the southward location of the sub-
tropical just. This will result in the storm beginning to struggle, with a weakening trend expected to begin by Friday
afternoon that will continue through landfall. Currently the storm is turning to the north, guided by strong high-pressure
ridging to the east. Over the coming days the storm will complete this turn to the north and continue until making
landfall in the southeastern United States near the coastal areas of Alabama and western Florida.
Latest ECMWF Valid Oct 9, 2026 at 12Z
